# Zapp — agent reference

> **Zapp is a desktop application framework.** Native code is written in Zen-C and
> compiled to a tiny binary (~450 KB for the JSC engine on macOS). The UI renders
> in the system WebView. The JavaScript side is your choice — plain HTML, Svelte,
> React, Vue, Solid, anything that builds through Vite.
>
> This document is the single source of truth for an agent building a Zapp app.
> It covers concepts, config shapes, the full runtime API, service signatures,
> common patterns, and the mistakes to avoid. No need to fetch anything else.
>
> **Platform:** macOS first. Windows in progress (portable framework with
> `#ifdef __APPLE__` stubs where Windows backends haven't landed).
> **Versions covered:** `@zappdev/cli`, `@zappdev/runtime`, `@zappdev/vite`
> each at `0.6.0-alpha.x`.

---

## Core concepts

### Two layers, three execution contexts

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Native binary (Zen-C → C11 → machine)     │
│     App ・ Window ・ Service ・ Menu ・ Notification │
│                      …Dock ・ Dialog                 │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────┘
               │ host objects          │ IPC (JSON)
               ▼                       ▼
    ┌────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────┐
    │   Workers          │   │   WebView (UI)       │
    │   (JS/TS threads)  │   │   HTML/CSS/JS        │
    │   headless OR      │   │   Vite-built         │
    │   webview-spawned  │   │                      │
    └────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────┘
```

**Native (Zen-C)** runs the app. It owns windows, services, menus, dock,
notifications, dialogs. Your entry point is `zapp/app.zc`.

**WebView** is the UI surface — what the user sees. One webview per window.
Uses WKWebView on macOS / WebView2 on Windows. Talks to native via a JSON
IPC bridge.

**Workers** are JavaScript threads with a fast direct-call bridge to native.
All workers share the same runtime API surface. They differ only by *how
they're spawned*:
- **Webview-spawned workers**: `new Worker("./my-worker.ts")` from inside
  a webview. Owner is the window that spawned them. Die when the window dies.
- **Headless workers**: declared in `zapp.config.ts` → `headless`. Start at
  app boot, no parent window, live for the app lifetime.

**No "backend worker" — that concept is gone.** All workers have full API
access: `Window.create`, `Events`, `Services`, `Notification`, `Dock`, `Sync`,
`App.quit`. The only thing you can't do from a worker is `Window.current()`
(you don't have a current window — you're not in one).

### When to use what

| Work | Where |
|---|---|
| UI (buttons, forms, layout) | Webview |
| Heavy JS compute (parse, crypto, image) | Webview-spawned Worker |
| App-level state that outlives any window | Headless worker |
| DB connection pool shared across windows | Headless worker |
| Long-running background sync / polling | Headless worker |
| Privileged native ops (FS, system info, menus) | Zen-C Service |

### Bridge IPC latency (for mental model)

Measured on M4 Max, `ping` round-trip:

| Path | Median | Throughput |
|---|---|---|
| Worker → native (direct host-object call) | ~5 µs | ~200k/s |
| Webview → native (WKWebView `userContentController`) | ~135 µs | ~7.4k/s |
| Electron renderer → main (reference) | ~52 µs | ~19k/s |

**Takeaway**: if you're making tight loops of IPC calls, do it from a worker,
not a webview. The WKWebView IPC can't be made faster — it's an OS-level
round-trip through WebKit's sandbox. Workers go straight to C.

---

## Project layout

What `bunx @zappdev/cli init my-app` scaffolds:

```
my-app/
├── package.json          # @zappdev/cli, runtime, vite as deps
├── zapp.config.ts        # app identity + headless + macOS opts
├── vite.config.ts        # auto-injects zappWorkers() from @zappdev/vite
├── tsconfig.json         # standard Vite TS setup
├── index.html            # webview entry
├── src/                  # your TS/UI code
│   └── main.ts
├── zapp/                 # your Zen-C (native) code
│   ├── app.zc            # run_app() — AppConfig, service registration, window
│   └── build.zc          # platform directives (frameworks, defines, link)
└── .zapp/                # CLI-generated, gitignored:
    ├── zapp_build_config.zc
    ├── zapp_platform.zc
    ├── zapp_bootstrap.zc
    ├── zapp_headless_workers.zc
    └── ...
```

**Yours to edit**: `zapp/app.zc`, `zapp/build.zc`, `zapp.config.ts`, `src/**`,
`index.html`, `vite.config.ts` (additional plugins).

**Don't edit**: `.zapp/**`, `bin/**`, `dist/**`, `release/**`. All generated.

### Scripts in package.json

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "zapp dev",       // Vite HMR + native compile + launch
    "build": "zapp build",   // production binary with embedded assets
    "package": "zapp package", // .app bundle with icon (macOS)
    "generate": "zapp generate" // regenerate TS bindings for services
  }
}
```

Run via `bun run dev`, `bun run build`, `bun run package`. Don't type
`zapp dev` directly — that hits a global install which may be stale. `bun run`
uses the local `node_modules/.bin/zapp`, guaranteed matching versions.

---

## AppConfig (zapp/app.zc)

The struct passed to `App::new(config)`. Every field required.

```zc
import "app/app.zc";

fn run_app() -> int {
    let config = AppConfig{
        name: "My App",
        applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed: true,
        webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_auto(),
        maxWorkers: 0,
        qjsStackSize: 0,
    };
    let app = App::new(config);
    app.service.add("greet", greet_handler);

    let opts = WindowOptions::create("My App");
    opts.width = 1200;
    opts.height = 800;
    opts.visible = false;
    let win = app.window.create(&opts);
    win.on_ready(on_ready);

    return app.run();
}

fn on_ready(_id: int, _handle: void*) -> void {
    Window{id: _id, handle: _handle}.show();
}
```

### Fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | App name (shown in menu bar, dock) |
| `applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed` | `bool` | macOS standard — quit when last window closes |
| `webContentInspectable` | `ZappInspectable` | Auto / On / Off — see below |
| `maxWorkers` | `int` | Upper bound on webview-spawned workers (0 = default 64) |
| `qjsStackSize` | `int` | QuickJS stack size for txiki workers (0 = default) |

### ZappInspectable enum

Controls whether the webview's "Inspect Element" is available.

```zc
// Preferred — convenience accessors
webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_auto(),  // dev → on, prod → off
webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_on(),    // always on
webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_off(),   // always off

// Equivalent raw form (less readable, prefer above)
webContentInspectable: ZappInspectable::Auto(),
webContentInspectable: ZappInspectable::On(),
webContentInspectable: ZappInspectable::Off(),
```

**Default for production apps**: `Zapp::inspectable_auto()`. Ships debug
tools in `zapp dev`, strips them in `zapp build` / `zapp package`.

### The `Zapp` namespace struct

A cross-cutting namespace for framework-level accessors that are scoped
under `Zapp::` so they don't pollute the global namespace. Today it holds
the three `inspectable_*` functions; future additions will go here.

### Service handler signature

```zc
fn my_service(_app: App*, _args: JsonValue*) -> string {
    // Parse args:
    if _args != NULL {
        let name_opt = _args.get_string("name");
        if name_opt.is_some() {
            let name = name_opt.unwrap();
            // ...
        }
    }

    // Return a JSON string. Use a _Thread_local buffer for fixed responses.
    raw {
        static _Thread_local char buf[128];
        snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "{\"greeting\":\"Hello %s\"}", "world");
        return buf;
    }
    return "";
}

// Register in run_app() before app.run():
app.service.add("greet", my_service);
```

**Always take `(App*, JsonValue*) -> string`**. Even if you don't use args,
use `_args: JsonValue*` and prefix with `_` to mark unused. Returning an empty
string signals "no response payload".

---

## zapp.config.ts

TypeScript config file at the project root. Typed via `defineConfig` from
`@zappdev/cli/config`.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@zappdev/cli/config";

export default defineConfig({
  name: "My App",
  identifier: "com.example.myapp",
  version: "1.0.0",

  // Headless workers — start at app boot, no parent window.
  // Keys are IDs (used for termination), values are source paths.
  headless: {
    db: "src/workers/db.ts",
    sync: "src/workers/sync.ts",
  },

  // Deep links: myapp://some/path opens the app with OPEN_URL event
  deepLinkSchemes: ["myapp"],

  // macOS-specific packaging opts
  macos: {
    icon: "assets/icon.png",     // converted to .icns at package time
    category: "public.app-category.developer-tools",
    minimumSystemVersion: "12.0",
    signingIdentity: undefined,  // undefined = adhoc signing
    acceptFirstMouse: true,
  },

  // Security — glob patterns for URLs the webview can navigate to
  security: {
    allowNavigation: ["https://myapi.example.com/*"],
  },
});
```

### Field reference

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required | App name (also appears in generated AppConfig if desired) |
| `identifier` | `string` | auto | Reverse-DNS bundle identifier |
| `version` | `string` | `"0.1.0"` | Semver, shown in About box / Info.plist |
| `assetDir` | `string` | `"./dist"` | Vite build output (usually don't change) |
| `devPort` | `number` | `5173` | Vite dev server port |
| `headless` | `Record<string,string>` | `{}` | Worker ID → source path map |
| `deepLinkSchemes` | `string[]` | `[]` | URL schemes to register |
| `macos.icon` | `string` | none | Path to `.png` / `.icns` / `.iconset` |
| `macos.signingIdentity` | `string` | adhoc | Apple Developer ID for signing |
| `security.allowNavigation` | `string[]` | none | Navigation allowlist (glob) |

---

## Runtime API (@zappdev/runtime)

All runtime APIs import from the same package. Same signatures everywhere —
webview, webview-spawned worker, headless worker. Under the hood, workers
take a zero-overhead direct path; webviews take the WKWebView IPC path.

```ts
import {
  App,
  Window, WindowEvent, type WindowHandle, type WindowOptions,
  Events, AppEvent,
  Services, type CancellablePromise,
  Worker, SharedWorker,
  Dialog,
  Menu, type MenuItemDef,
  ContextMenu,
  Notification, type NotificationOptions,
  Sync,
  Dock,
} from "@zappdev/runtime";
```

### App

```ts
App.quit(): void
App.openExternal(url: string): void   // open in system browser
App.on(event: AppEvent, handler): () => void
App.getConfig(): Record<string, unknown>  // bootstrapped config
```

### Events

Global event bus. Events fire locally; `emit()` from a worker broadcasts
to every webview, and from a webview is local-only.

```ts
Events.on(name: string, handler: (payload) => void): () => void
Events.emit(name: string, payload?: Record<string, unknown>): void
eventName(event: WindowEvent | AppEvent): string  // enum → string name
```

**WindowEvent enum** (0–10):
`READY, FOCUS, BLUR, RESIZE, MOVE, CLOSE, MINIMIZE, MAXIMIZE, RESTORE,
FULLSCREEN, UNFULLSCREEN`

**AppEvent enum** (100+):
`STARTED (100), SHUTDOWN (101), REOPEN (104), OPEN_URL (105),
DID_BECOME_ACTIVE (106), DID_RESIGN_ACTIVE (107)`

STARTED / SHUTDOWN fire before/after any webview exists — handle them in a
headless worker if you need to react.

### Window

```ts
// Webview only — throws in workers
Window.current(): WindowHandle

// Everywhere. In workers: direct C call via __zappBridge.createWindow.
// In webview: async __window:create invoke over IPC.
Window.create(opts?: Partial<WindowOptions>): Promise<WindowHandle>
```

`WindowHandle`:
```ts
readonly id: string
on(event: WindowEvent, handler): () => void  // scoped to this window
show() / hide() / close()
setTitle(title) / setSize(w, h) / setPosition(x, y)
minimize() / maximize()
setFullscreen(on) / setAlwaysOnTop(on)
setCloseGuard(on)   // when true, CLOSE event fires and close is blocked until close()
loadUrl(url)
```

`WindowOptions`:
```ts
{
  title?: string
  url?: string
  width?: number
  height?: number
  x?: number
  y?: number
  visible?: boolean
  resizable?: boolean
  closable?: boolean
  minimizable?: boolean
  maximizable?: boolean
  fullscreen?: boolean
  borderless?: boolean
  transparent?: boolean
  alwaysOnTop?: boolean
  titleBarStyle?: "default" | "hidden" | "hiddenInset"
}
```

### Services

Call Zen-C service handlers registered via `app.service.add(name, fn)`.

```ts
Services.invoke<T>(method: string, args?: object, opts?: { timeout? }): CancellablePromise<T>
Services.invokeSync<T>(method: string, args?: object): T   // workers only
```

`CancellablePromise<T>` has `.cancel()` to abort a pending invoke.

**In webview**: async IPC round-trip (~135 µs).
**In worker**: direct host-object C call (~5 µs), returned as resolved Promise.
**`invokeSync`**: worker-only. Throws if called from a webview.

### Notification

Full feature: permission, show, schedule, actions (buttons/reply), update,
cancel, remove from Notification Center.

```ts
Notification.requestPermission(): Promise<PermissionStatus>
Notification.getPermissionStatus(): Promise<PermissionStatus>
Notification.show(options): Promise<id>
Notification.schedule(options with trigger): Promise<id>
Notification.cancel(id) / cancelAll()
Notification.removeDelivered(id) / removeAllDelivered()
Notification.update(id, options)
Notification.registerCategory(category)   // webview only — needs typed struct args
Notification.removeCategory(id)
Notification.on("response" | "click" | "action", handler): () => void
```

`NotificationOptions`:
```ts
{
  title: string
  subtitle?: string
  body?: string
  sound?: "default" | "none" | string
  threadId?: string
  categoryId?: string        // must registerCategory first
  data?: Record<string, unknown>
  attachment?: string        // file path or file:// URL
  id?: string                // explicit ID for update/removeDelivered
}
```

`PermissionStatus`: `"granted" | "denied" | "not-determined" | "provisional"`

**macOS requires**: app bundle + code signing. `zapp dev` handles this
automatically with adhoc signing; `zapp package` respects `macos.signingIdentity`.

### Dock (macOS)

```ts
Dock.showIcon() / hideIcon()
Dock.setBadge(label: string) / removeBadge()
Dock.bounce(type?: "informational" | "critical")
Dock.setIcon(path: string) / resetIcon()
```

### Menu

```ts
Menu.build(items: MenuItemDef[]): MenuHandle
```

`MenuItemDef`:
```ts
{
  id?: string
  label?: string
  type?: "normal" | "separator" | "checkbox"
  enabled?: boolean
  checked?: boolean
  accelerator?: string   // e.g. "CmdOrCtrl+N"
  role?: "editMenu" | "windowMenu" | "appMenu" | "copy" | "cut" | "paste"
       | "selectAll" | "undo" | "redo" | "quit"
  action?: () => void    // fires on click
  submenu?: MenuItemDef[]
}
```

Roles automatically supply the right system items. `role: "editMenu"`
creates the whole Edit menu.

### ContextMenu

One-shot native context menu.

```ts
ContextMenu.show(items: MenuItemDef[], options?: { x?: number, y?: number }): void
```

Without `x`/`y`, uses the last `contextmenu` event position. Action listeners
are auto-cleaned after click or 30 s timeout.

### Dialog

Native file and message dialogs. All async.

```ts
Dialog.openFile(opts?: OpenFileOptions): Promise<{ cancelled, paths? }>
Dialog.saveFile(opts?: SaveFileOptions): Promise<{ cancelled, path? }>
Dialog.message(opts: MessageOptions): Promise<{ button: number }>
```

`MessageOptions`:
```ts
{
  message: string
  title?: string
  kind?: "info" | "warning" | "critical"
  buttons?: string[]    // defaults to ["OK"]
}
```

### Sync — cross-context wait/notify

Low-level coordination across windows/workers. Like `pthread_cond_*` but
keyed by string.

```ts
Sync.wait(key: string, timeoutMs?: number | null): Promise<"notified" | "timed-out">
Sync.notify(key: string, count = 1): void    // wake N waiters (default 1)
Sync.notifyAll(key: string): void              // wake all waiters
```

Useful for: rate-limiting a resource to one waiter at a time, draining a
queue on a signal, any race between background producer and foreground
consumer.

### Worker / SharedWorker

Spawn from a webview.

```ts
const w = new Worker("./path/to/worker.ts");
w.postMessage({ task: "compute" });
w.onmessage = (e) => console.log(e.data);
w.send("channel", payload);            // named channel (typed routing)
w.receive("channel", handler);         // unsub = receive returns
w.terminate();

const sw = new SharedWorker("./shared.ts");  // URL-keyed, refcounted
sw.port.postMessage(...);
```

Workers have the full runtime API. They are *not* web workers in the
standard sense — they're Zapp workers with a privileged bridge. `fetch`
and timers need the txiki engine (not JSC).

---

## Worker engines

Zen-C's `zapp/build.zc` chooses which engine to compile in.

```zc
// JSC — macOS only, ~450 KB binary, no web APIs in workers (no fetch, no
// WebSocket, but setTimeout/clearTimeout are provided by Zapp).
//> macos: define: ZAPP_WORKER_ENGINE_JSC

// txiki.js — cross-platform, ~6.5 MB binary, full web APIs (fetch,
// WebSocket, timers, Performance, etc.). CLI downloads + builds it on
// first use (~60 s one-time cost). Uses a patched fork via the
// cookie-jar-path upstream gap.
//> macos: define: ZAPP_WORKER_ENGINE_TXIKI
```

Pick **one** engine per app. Both can't be active at once.

- **JSC** when: macOS-only app, want the smallest possible binary, don't need
  fetch/WebSocket *inside workers* (you can still do fetch/WebSocket in the
  webview — the UI has full DOM APIs).
- **txiki** when: cross-platform, want web APIs inside workers, size budget
  allows ~6 MB. Also required for Windows.

---

## Common patterns

### Close guard — "unsaved changes?" dialog

```ts
// src/main.ts (webview)
import { Window, WindowEvent, Dialog } from "@zappdev/runtime";

const win = Window.current();
win.setCloseGuard(true);

win.on(WindowEvent.CLOSE, async () => {
  const result = await Dialog.message({
    message: "Save changes before closing?",
    buttons: ["Save", "Don't save", "Cancel"],
  });
  if (result.button === 0) {
    await save();
    win.close();                 // explicit close, bypasses guard
  } else if (result.button === 1) {
    win.close();
  }
  // button 2 = stay open
});
```

### Headless worker with broadcast

```ts
// zapp.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  name: "my-app",
  headless: { sync: "src/workers/sync.ts" },
});
```

```ts
// src/workers/sync.ts
import { Events, Services } from "@zappdev/runtime";

setInterval(async () => {
  const latest = await Services.invoke("fetchLatest");
  Events.emit("data:updated", latest);   // broadcast to every open webview
}, 5000);
```

```ts
// src/main.ts (webview — any window can listen)
import { Events } from "@zappdev/runtime";

Events.on("data:updated", (data) => {
  render(data);
});
```

### Service with lifecycle (startup / shutdown)

```zc
import "app/app.zc";

struct CounterService {
    value: int;
}

let counter = CounterService{value: 0};

fn counter_startup(ptr: void*) -> void {
    let self = (CounterService*)ptr;
    self.value = 0;
    println "counter started";
}

fn counter_shutdown(ptr: void*) -> void {
    println "counter stopped";
}

fn counter_increment(_app: App*, _args: JsonValue*) -> string {
    counter.value = counter.value + 1;
    raw {
        static _Thread_local char buf[64];
        snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "{\"value\":%d}", counter.value);
        return buf;
    }
    return "";
}

fn run_app() -> int {
    let config = AppConfig{
        name: "counter",
        applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed: true,
        webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_auto(),
        maxWorkers: 0,
        qjsStackSize: 0,
    };
    let app = App::new(config);

    // register() gives you lifecycle hooks (startup/shutdown).
    // add() is the shortcut when you don't need them.
    app.service.register("increment", (void*)&counter, &ServiceImpl{
        handler: counter_increment,
        startup: counter_startup,
        shutdown: counter_shutdown,
    });

    let opts = WindowOptions::create("counter");
    opts.visible = false;
    let win = app.window.create(&opts);
    win.on_ready(fn (_id: int, _handle: void*) -> void {
        Window{id: _id, handle: _handle}.show();
    });

    return app.run();
}
```

### Notification with action buttons

```ts
import { Notification } from "@zappdev/runtime";

// One-time: register the category
await Notification.registerCategory({
  id: "message",
  actions: [
    { id: "reply", title: "Reply" },
    { id: "delete", title: "Delete", destructive: true },
  ],
  hasReplyField: true,
  replyPlaceholder: "Type your reply...",
  replyButtonTitle: "Send",
});

// Show one
await Notification.show({
  title: "New message from Alice",
  body: "Hey, are you free?",
  categoryId: "message",
});

// React — these fire for any category
Notification.on("response", (r) => {
  console.log("notif", r.id, "action:", r.actionId, "text:", r.userText);
});
```

### Menu with actions

```ts
import { Menu, App } from "@zappdev/runtime";

Menu.build([
  { role: "appMenu" },
  { label: "File", submenu: [
    { label: "New", accelerator: "CmdOrCtrl+N", action: () => newFile() },
    { label: "Open", accelerator: "CmdOrCtrl+O", action: () => openFile() },
    { type: "separator" },
    { label: "Quit", accelerator: "CmdOrCtrl+Q", action: () => App.quit() },
  ]},
  { label: "Edit", role: "editMenu" },
  { label: "Window", role: "windowMenu" },
]);
```

---

## Anti-patterns

### Don't use `backend: bool` in AppConfig

Removed in 0.6.0-alpha.0. Previously you'd set `backend: true` to enable a
singleton privileged JS worker. Now: declare headless workers explicitly in
`zapp.config.ts` under `headless`. The unified worker model means each
worker is explicit about its purpose and ID.

```ts
// WRONG (AppConfig field no longer exists)
AppConfig{ backend: true, ... }

// RIGHT (declare in zapp.config.ts)
export default defineConfig({ headless: { main: "src/main-worker.ts" } });
```

### Don't use raw `webContentInspectable: -1 / 0 / 1`

Field is now a `ZappInspectable` enum. Use the `Zapp::inspectable_*()`
accessors.

```zc
// WRONG
webContentInspectable: -1

// RIGHT
webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_auto()
```

### Don't `await Window.create()` at module top in a webview

Webview context doesn't have the worker fast path — it goes through async
IPC. Top-level await is fine in a worker (direct C call, synchronous under
the hood), but in a webview you should wrap in an async handler:

```ts
// WRONG (webview) — IPC not ready at module init
const w = await Window.create({...});

// RIGHT
async function openSecondaryWindow() {
  const w = await Window.create({...});
}
button.addEventListener("click", openSecondaryWindow);
```

In a headless worker, top-level `await Window.create(...)` is fine — workers
are ready before your code runs.

### Don't use `Window.current()` from a worker

Workers have no "current" window. Use `Window.create` to spawn a new one, or
pass `windowId` through a service call if you need to operate on a specific
existing window.

```ts
// WRONG (from worker)
const w = Window.current();   // throws

// RIGHT
const w = await Window.create({...});
```

### Don't assume workers have a different API

Same `import { Window, Events, ... } from "@zappdev/runtime"` imports work
in all three contexts. Internal fast paths are automatic. If some code runs
in both a webview and a worker, write it once and trust the runtime.

### Don't type `zapp dev` in your terminal

Use `bun run dev` (or the other scripts). Bare `zapp` hits a global install
(which may be stale or missing); `bun run` resolves to the local
`node_modules/.bin/zapp` pinned in your project's `package.json`.

### Don't block the main thread in a service handler

Service handlers run on the native thread that received the call (worker
thread in worker-context, main thread in webview-context). Long ops (big
file reads, network, crypto) should run async or on a background thread. A
10 ms blocking service freezes the UI for 10 ms.

### Production security — use `inspectable_off()` if you don't want devtools

`Zapp::inspectable_auto()` turns devtools off in `zapp build` / `zapp package`
(production mode). If you want belt-and-suspenders certainty, or you ship
a `zapp dev` build to internal users, use `Zapp::inspectable_off()` to hard-
disable devtools regardless of build mode.

---

## CLI — @zappdev/cli

Commands (via `bun run <script>` in a project):

| Command | Scaffolds / Builds |
|---|---|
| `zapp init <name> [-t template]` | New project (vanilla-ts, svelte-ts, react-ts, vue-ts, etc.) |
| `zapp dev` | Vite HMR + native compile + launch. Watches `zapp/**` for recompile. |
| `zapp build` | Production binary in `bin/`. Embeds Vite `dist/` as brotli-compressed assets. |
| `zapp package` | macOS `.app` bundle in `release/` with icon + Info.plist + adhoc signing. |
| `zapp generate` | Scan `app.service.add(...)` calls, emit TS bindings for Services.invoke. |

Flags:
- `--verbose` / `-v`: stream full `zc`/`clang` output. Without this, only
  errors are shown (~200 framework warnings are suppressed).
- `-r <path>`: run in a different project directory.

First `zapp dev` / `zapp build` with `ZAPP_WORKER_ENGINE_TXIKI` defined
clones + builds txiki.js (~60 s one-time). Cached in `~/.zapp/vendor/txiki.js`.

---

## Vite plugin — @zappdev/vite

Scaffolded `vite.config.ts` wires it up automatically. The plugin:

1. Scans source for `new Worker("./foo.ts")` patterns, bundles each as a
   separate entry to `dist/_workers/foo.mjs`, rewrites the import to the
   output URL.
2. Bundles headless workers declared in `zapp.config.ts` to
   `dist/_workers/_headless_<id>.mjs` — native code loads them at boot.
3. Provides a dev middleware that serves `/_workers/*` from
   `.zapp/workers/` so the WebView's `new Worker()` calls resolve during
   `zapp dev`.

Options (mostly auto-configured):

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { zappWorkers } from "@zappdev/vite";
import zappConfig from "./zapp.config";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    zappWorkers({ headless: zappConfig.headless }),
    // your other plugins (svelte(), react(), etc.)
  ],
});
```

---

## Packaging and distribution

### Icons

Pass `macos.icon` in `zapp.config.ts` as a path to a `.png`, `.icns`, or
`.iconset`. The CLI builds the appropriate macOS asset catalog on package.
On macOS 14+ (Sonoma) with a PNG, the icon gets a "liquid glass" treatment
automatically.

Recommended: 1024×1024 PNG. The CLI generates all the required resolutions.

### Signing

Adhoc signing (the default) produces a `.app` that runs locally but will
show "unidentified developer" warnings elsewhere. For distribution, set
`macos.signingIdentity` to your Apple Developer certificate name:

```ts
macos: { signingIdentity: "Developer ID Application: Your Name (TEAMID)" }
```

Notarization is not automated yet — you'll want to run `xcrun notarytool`
against the produced `.app` bundle.

### Binary size

A trivial "hello world" — one window, one service:

| Engine | Binary | Bundle (with icon) |
|---|---|---|
| JSC | ~450 KB | ~3 MB (2.4 MB is the multi-resolution icon) |
| txiki | ~6.5 MB | ~9 MB |

The icon dominates the JSC bundle. Without icon, zapp-jsc ships in ~460 KB.

---

## Quick-start template

For agents: what a minimal Zapp app looks like from scratch.

`zapp.config.ts`:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@zappdev/cli/config";

export default defineConfig({
  name: "hello",
  identifier: "com.example.hello",
  version: "0.1.0",
});
```

`zapp/app.zc`:
```zc
import "app/app.zc";
import "std/time.zc";

fn now_ms(_app: App*, _args: JsonValue*) -> string {
    let ms = Time::now();
    raw {
        static _Thread_local char buf[64];
        snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "{\"now\":%llu}", (unsigned long long)ms);
        return buf;
    }
    return "";
}

fn on_ready(_id: int, _handle: void*) -> void {
    Window{id: _id, handle: _handle}.show();
}

fn run_app() -> int {
    let config = AppConfig{
        name: "hello",
        applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed: true,
        webContentInspectable: Zapp::inspectable_auto(),
        maxWorkers: 0,
        qjsStackSize: 0,
    };
    let app = App::new(config);
    app.service.add("now", now_ms);

    let opts = WindowOptions::create("hello");
    opts.width = 600;
    opts.height = 400;
    opts.visible = false;
    let win = app.window.create(&opts);
    win.on_ready(on_ready);

    return app.run();
}
```

`zapp/build.zc`:
```zc
//> macos: define: apple
//> windows: define: windows

//> macos: define: ZAPP_WORKER_ENGINE_JSC

//> macos: framework: Cocoa
//> macos: framework: WebKit
//> macos: framework: CoreFoundation
//> macos: framework: JavaScriptCore
//> macos: framework: Security
//> macos: framework: UserNotifications
//> macos: link: -lcompression
//> macos: cflags: -fobjc-arc -x objective-c

//> windows: cflags: -DUNICODE -D_UNICODE -DCINTERFACE -DCOBJMACROS
//> windows: link: -lole32 -lshell32 -luuid -luser32 -lgdi32 -lcomctl32 -lcomdlg32 -lshlwapi
//> windows: link: -lwinhttp -lbcrypt -ladvapi32 -lrpcrt4 -lcrypt32 -lversion

import "app.zc";

fn main() -> int {
    return run_app();
}
```

`src/main.ts`:
```ts
import { Window, WindowEvent, Services } from "@zappdev/runtime";

const win = Window.current();
win.on(WindowEvent.READY, () => win.show());

document.body.innerHTML = `
  <main>
    <h1>Hello Zapp</h1>
    <button id="now">Get server time</button>
    <pre id="out"></pre>
  </main>
`;

document.getElementById("now")!.addEventListener("click", async () => {
  const r = await Services.invoke<{ now: number }>("now");
  document.getElementById("out")!.textContent = `now = ${r.now}`;
});
```

Run: `bun install && bun run dev`. Ship: `bun run package`.
